items.title: AMF sends Registration Accept after a failed NAS integrity check, skipping the authentication and security recovery required for a mobility update
items.body:
## Summary

OAI AMF at revision `b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7` accepts a Mobility Registration Request whose NAS MAC fails verification. The UE starts from a completed registration, enters CM-IDLE, and sends the request as the first NAS message on a new connection. The AMF detects the MAC mismatch, processes the inner request through its cleartext-recovery branch, and sends Registration Accept using the existing NAS security context. It skips the authentication, NAS Security Mode Control, and initial-message retransmission required by TS 33.501 §6.4.6.

The UE then sends a valid Registration Complete and, after another connection release, a valid Service Request. Both pass AMF integrity verification; the AMF processes completion and sends Service Accept.

## Environment

- AMF revision: `b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7`.
- Deployed AMF image tag: `oai-amf:upstream-v2.2.2`; its revision label identifies the commit above.
- Companion core NFs: OAI v2.2.1.
- Client: modified UERANSIM v3.2.6 with explicit NAS input control; source baseline `fd694e2928162572df58160dc1b3ad337c0a52df` plus the registration-request MAC mutation below.
- Negotiated NAS algorithms: NIA1 and NEA0.
- Topology: one AMF, gNB, and test UE; normal registration followed by a mobility update.
- Trial date: 21 October 2026. Correct-MAC control: `1good-r3`; invalid-MAC trial: `1bad-r3`.

## Reproduction

1. Complete initial registration: Registration Request → Authentication Request/Response → Security Mode Command/Complete → Registration Accept/Complete. Confirm `5GMM-REGISTERED` at the AMF.

2. Release the UE connection and wait for CM-IDLE.

3. Build a Mobility Registration Request with registration type `2`, identity `5G-GUTI`, ngKSI `2`, and outer SHT `1`, using the current NAS security context.

4. After NAS MAC calculation and encoding, flip one bit of the first MAC octet, immediately before sending the PDU to RRC:

   ```cpp
   pdu.data()[2] ^= 0x01;
   ```

   The transmitted NAS header is `7E 01 6E 69 FE 9F 02`. The AMF calculates `6F69FE9F` and receives `6E69FE9F`.

5. Send the request through NGAP InitialUEMessage and observe Registration Accept as its direct response.

6. Send Registration Complete using the current NAS keys. Observe `Integrity matched` and `REGISTRATION_COMPLETE_RECEIVED` at the AMF.

7. Release the connection, wait for CM-IDLE, and send a valid Service Request. Observe Service Accept at the UE and `SERVICE_ACCEPT_SENT` at the AMF.

Run the same sequence with the normally generated MAC as a control. The harness input sequence and both output sequences are included in `reproducer.txt` and `results.json`.

## Observed behavior

The target request in `1bad-r3` was sent at `2026-10-21T15:26:09.828545Z`. The next NAS response was Registration Accept at `15:26:09.829407Z`.

| Stage                                           | Correct MAC                             | Invalid MAC                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Target mobility request                         | Integrity matched → Registration Accept | MAC mismatch → cleartext recovery → Registration Accept |
| Target authentication and Security Mode Control | Existing-context fast path              | Authentication and SMC skipped                          |
| Registration Complete                           | Integrity matched; processed            | Integrity matched; processed                            |
| Subsequent Service Request                      | Service Accept                          | Integrity matched → Service Accept                      |

The AMF logs the following events for the invalid-MAC request, in order:

```text
Dropping uplink NAS message: MAC mismatch (computed 0x6f69fe9f, received 0x6e69fe9f)
Inner type 0x41: processing as cleartext (do not store uplink COUNT, recovery procedures apply)
Handling Mobility Registration Update...
Size of Registration Accept message 55
```

The capture records the target request in frames `71/72`, Registration Accept in `73/74`, and Registration Complete in `79/80`. Each adjacent pair represents the same SCTP TSN captured on two interfaces by `tcpdump -i any`. With negotiated NEA0, the NAS message types in the SHT=2 bodies are directly decodable.

The AMF subsequently records `Integrity matched` and `REGISTRATION_COMPLETE_RECEIVED` at `15:26:10.432–10.433Z`. At `15:26:12.268–12.270Z`, it verifies the Service Request and records `SERVICE_ACCEPT_SENT`; the UE records Service Accept. The packet CSV establishes the request/Accept/Complete exchange; the UE and AMF logs establish the later service exchange.

## Required behavior

[TS 24.501 V17.10.1 §4.4.4.3, printed page 59](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/124500_124599/124501/17.10.01_60/ts_124501v171001p.pdf#page=60) provides recovery handling for certain initial NAS messages whose MAC fails or cannot be verified. This permits the AMF to identify the Registration Request and enter recovery.

[TS 33.501 V17.10.0 §6.4.6, printed pages 66–67](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/133500_133599/133501/17.10.00_60/ts_133501v171000p.pdf#page=68) defines the required recovery: Step 2 starts authentication after an integrity failure; Step 3 sends SMC after successful authentication and requests retransmission of the complete initial message; Step 4 carries that message in a protected Security Mode Complete; Step 5 responds. The idle-to-connected mobility request here is an initial NAS message under this definition. The applicable requirement is recovery before Registration Accept.

## Source path

References are pinned to the tested AMF revision:

1. [amf_n1.cpp:499–524](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7/src/amf-app/amf_n1.cpp#L499-L524): failed verification of the integrity-protected request reaches the plaintext allowlist; the inner message becomes the decoded input for further processing.
2. [amf_n1.cpp:586–603](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7/src/amf-app/amf_n1.cpp#L586-L603): Registration Request is an allowed message type for that recovery branch.
3. [amf_n1.cpp:5036–5077](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7/src/amf-app/amf_n1.cpp#L5036-L5077): the mobility handler selects the registration procedure when the security-context object is absent. An existing object selects construction of Registration Accept. This decision uses context presence after the triggering request has failed integrity verification.
4. [amf_n1.cpp:5151–5239](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7/src/amf-app/amf_n1.cpp#L5151-L5239): the handler protects the Accept with the existing context and sends it through NAS transport or Initial Context Setup.

## Security impact

An integrity-failed mobility registration request drives the registration-update acceptance path under an existing subscriber context. The AMF bypasses the authentication and NAS security recovery required for that failed request. This is a request-authentication and recovery bypass.

The subsequent valid completion and service messages succeed under the established UE/AMF context. These exchanges demonstrate continued NAS operation after the AMF has accepted the integrity-failed request. The test UE performs this continuation with its established NAS keys.


## Evidence



The ZIP contains four files: `events.log` with time-aligned UE/gNB/AMF excerpts and original line numbers; `packet-sequence.csv` with decoded NAS/NGAP fields and original capture frame numbers; `results.json` with trial outputs and version information; and `reproducer.txt` with the input sequence and MAC mutation.

[oai-mobility-integrity-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33801050/oai-mobility-integrity-evidence.zip)

items.title: AMF accepts registration updates but rejects valid Registration Complete
items.body:
## Summary

OAI AMF v2.2.2 accepts a registration update while its mobility-management state remains DEREGISTERED, then rejects the corresponding Registration Complete with cause 101. The Complete passes NAS integrity verification. The same update path also accepts a plaintext SHT=0 request using an existing security context, with integrity verification of the triggering request and authentication recovery omitted.

The starting condition is an initial Registration Accept containing a GUTI whose confirmation is still pending. The UE has entered REGISTERED locally, while the AMF is waiting for Registration Complete. A Service Reject with cause 101 changes the AMF to DEREGISTERED; the UE continues in REGISTERED with its existing GUTI and NAS security context. A subsequent registration update receives another Accept, followed by rejection of its valid Complete.

This produces two connected failures: an unprotected request drives registration-update processing, and an accepted update has a broken completion path.

## Triggering path and observed results

Execute the following NAS input sequence from a fresh core/gNB/UE session. Send the Service Request while confirmation of the first Registration Accept is still pending.

```text
registrationRequest
→ authenticationResponse
→ securityModeComplete
→ serviceRequest
→ registrationRequest (configuration under test)
```

The observed responses are:

```text
authenticationRequest
→ securityModeCommand
→ registrationAccept
→ serviceReject (cause 101)
→ registrationAccept
```

The last input is a Registration Request with the identity, registration type and security header selected from the table below. The harness command for the GUTI identity is `registrationRequestGUTI`.

| Identity     | Registration type  | Uplink SHT | Target response     |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ---------- | ------------------- |
| SUCI or GUTI | 2: mobility update | 0, 1, 2    | Registration Accept |
| SUCI or GUTI | 3: periodic update | 1          | Registration Accept |

Every listed variant receives an Accept with outer SHT=2. Sending `registrationComplete` immediately afterwards produces `registrationReject` with cause 101. The AMF remains DEREGISTERED, and the Complete passes NAS integrity verification.

The representative GUTI/type2/SHT0 and SHT1 cases exercise connection release and re-establishment before the target request. The connection's 5G-S-TMSI identifies the existing AMF/NAS context.

For SHT=0, the AMF proceeds directly to the update Accept using the existing keys, skipping current-request integrity verification, a new authentication procedure, and security-mode recovery. For SHT=1, both the request and its Complete pass integrity verification, and the AMF still rejects completion because its state is DEREGISTERED.

An initial-registration control (type 1) instead receives Authentication Request at the target step, enters authentication and security-mode control, completes registration, and subsequently receives Service Accept.

[public-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33621595/public-evidence.zip)

## Source analysis

The following references use AMF commit `b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7`.

1. **The context survives connection release.** The N2 release-complete handler removes the NGAP association while keeping the AMF/NAS context available for the next connection: [amf_n2.cpp, lines 1762–1770](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7/src/amf-app/amf_n2.cpp#L1762-L1770).
2. **Service Reject changes the AMF state.** `service_request_handle()` returns cause 101 for the pending-registration state. `send_service_reject(nc, cause)` dispatches `SERVICE_REJECT_SENT`, moving the AMF to DEREGISTERED while the security context remains available: [amf_n1.cpp, lines 1415–1426](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7/src/amf-app/amf_n1.cpp#L1415-L1426), [lines 1883–1887](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7/src/amf-app/amf_n1.cpp#L1883-L1887).
3. **The update handler checks a transition but leaves it uncommitted.** `run_mobility_registration_update_procedure()` calls `check_nas_event(REGISTRATION_REQUEST_RECEIVED)`, then uses the presence of `security_ctx` to select the direct-Accept path. It creates an Accept containing a GUTI while omitting the associated state transition and T3550 setup: [amf_n1.cpp, lines 5036–5239](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7/src/amf-app/amf_n1.cpp#L5036-L5239). `check_nas_event()` validates a possible transition; state mutation belongs to the event-handling path: [nas_state_machine.cpp, lines 282–296](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7/src/amf-app/nas_state_machine.cpp#L282-L296). The periodic-update handlers have the same omission.
4. **The plaintext-request path reaches the same acceptance decision.** SHT=0 Registration Request passes the plaintext allowlist. The update handler bases acceptance on the existing security-context object rather than successful authentication of this request: [amf_n1.cpp, lines 479–590](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7/src/amf-app/amf_n1.cpp#L479-L590), [lines 5060–5076](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7/src/amf-app/amf_n1.cpp#L5060-L5076).
5. **Complete reaches the stale state.** `registration_complete_handle()` sees DEREGISTERED and returns cause 101. The code that stops T3550 and commits registration completion lies after this failed state check: [amf_n1.cpp, lines 4109–4151](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7/src/amf-app/amf_n1.cpp#L4109-L4151).

The resulting inconsistency is between the acceptance decision, request authentication, and the AMF state required to complete the accepted procedure.

## Expected behavior and security significance

[TS 24.501 §5.5.1.3.4](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/124500_124599/124501/17.10.01_60/ts_124501v171001p.pdf#page=340) requires the AMF to start T3550 and enter COMMON-PROCEDURE-INITIATED when an update Accept contains a GUTI. On the corresponding Complete, the AMF stops T3550 and enters REGISTERED. The observed DEREGISTERED → Accept → rejected Complete behavior violates this required progression.

[TS 33.501 §6.4.6](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/133500_133599/133501/17.10.00_60/ts_133501v171000p.pdf#page=67) defines authentication and security establishment for initial NAS messages. Existing keys identify an available security context; verification of the current request establishes its authenticity. The SHT=0 case skips that distinction and allows an unprotected request to drive update processing and a protected response. Encrypting and authenticating the response protects the response itself; the triggering request still requires authentication.

For SHT=0, the AMF processes the update using an existing context while skipping current-request integrity verification and a new authentication procedure. The state-management impact is rejection of a valid completion message after the AMF has accepted the update, disrupting registration recovery.

## Affected version and evidence

- AMF: v2.2.2, commit `b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7`.
- common-src: `c0dcc9aa70da170b3dcd690a34e704be4199f3fd`.
- Deployment: official-revision AMF build, image `oai-amf:upstream-v2.2.2`; companion core NFs v2.2.1.
- Test client: modified UERANSIM v3.2.6 with explicit NAS input control.
- Environment: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-138-generic, 4 virtual CPUs on AMD Ryzen 7 9700X, approximately 7.7 GiB RAM and 38.7 GiB disk; Docker 29.6.2 and Compose v5.3.1.

`public-evidence.zip` contains the triggering path, tested configurations, representative decoded fields, short AMF event excerpts, source references, and version information. Test-harness commands and full selected NAS traces are prepared in `maintainer-details.zip` for maintainer follow-up.

items.title: Second UE-triggered Service Request after AN UP deactivate: UL UP does not come back (no SMF SR step 1 / UL PDR)
items.body:
After a successful CM-IDLE -> UE-triggered Service Request recovery, a second real UP deactivate + MO Service Request against OAI CN5G leaves control plane OK but UL user plane dead (100% ping loss).

Cycle 1 works. From cycle 2:
1) AMF sends Service Accept + Initial Context Setup without repeating the SMF update with `upCnxState: ACTIVATING`.
2) SMF never runs `Service Request (UE-triggered, step 1)`
3) SMF treats the N2 path like PDU session establishment
4) UPF ends with DL PDR only (no UL)

## Reproduction

1. OAI CN5G (CI pipeline `container_5g_rfsim_24prb` in https://github.com/duranta-project/openairinterface5g/pull/520 as reference)
2. Add multiple idle hops in a row: i.e. `rrc ctx_rel_req`, or run locally
3. First triggered UL (ping) -> MO Service Request -> ping OK (cycle 1)
4. Repeat step 2–3 -> CP OK again, ping 100% loss (cycle 2)

## Observed behaviour

**Cycle 1 (works):** After Service Request, AMF asks SMF to activate user plane (`upCnxState: ACTIVATING`). SMF runs UE-triggered Service Request (step 1 + 2), allocates an UL F-TEID, and UPF installs both UL and DL forwarding. Ping succeeds.

**Cycle 2 (fails):** AMF still sends Service Accept and Initial Context Setup, but does not ask SMF to activate UP again. SMF never runs Service Request step 1, it treats the N2 info like a PDU session establishment and marks UP active anyway. UPF gets only DL rules, no UL. The gNB often reuses the old UL TEID, which UPF no longer handles -> **100% UL ping loss**.

On both releases (noise): AMF to SMF HTTP/JSON around UP deactivate looks broken (`Couldn't get the HTTP response` / empty JSON) even though SMF did deactivate on N4. SMF may also log `Unknown session procedure type` after AN-initiated release.

## Expected behaviour

On every UE-triggered Service Request after UP was deactivated, AMF should again drive SMF with the Service Request / `ACTIVATING` path so SMF runs SR step 1 (UL F-TEID) and UPF installs UL + DL PDRs.

## Logs

[ci-scripts_yaml_files_5g_rfsimulator_24prb__.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32048425/ci-scripts_yaml_files_5g_rfsimulator_24prb__.zip)

items.title: [Bug]: AMF crash via truncated SUCI in NAS Registration Request (Pre-authentication DoS)
items.body:
### Description

A pre-authentication denial-of-service vulnerability exists in the OAI  CN5G AMF NAS decoder. A malformed **5GS Mobile Identity IE** containing a truncated SUCI can  trigger an integer underflow in `DecodeSuci()`. The resulting negative  length is converted into an unsigned value, causing an out-of-bounds heap read. By sending crafted NAS Registration Requests through  NGAP/SCTP, a rogue gNB can crash the AMF process.

The vulnerability is reachable before authentication and does not  require:
- A valid SIM card
- A provisioned subscriber
- NAS security context
- Successful authentication

### Affected Component
Tested Image: `oaisoftwarealliance/oai-amf:v2.2.1`
Affected code path:
```
RegistrationRequest::Decode
        |
        |_5gsMobileIdentity::DecodeSuci
                |
                decode_bstring()
                        |
                        blk2bstr()
```

### Root Cause

The vulnerability is caused by insufficient length validation when  decoding the 5GS Mobile Identity IE.

`Type6NasIe::Validate()` only checks whether the declared IE length exceeds the available buffer size. It does not enforce a minimum length  
before parsing the SUCI content.

A truncated SUCI with `ie_len = 7` is accepted and passed to `DecodeSuci()`.
The decoder then parses a fixed 8-byte SUCI layout: `ecoded_size = 8` and calculates:
```
scheme_output_length = ie_len - decoded_size;
                     = 7 - 8;
                     = -1;
```
The negative value is passed to `decode_bstring()` as unsigned  parameters:
```
pdulen = 65535
buflen = 4294967295
```
The internal length validation is bypassed and `blk2bstr()` performs: `memcpy(..., 65535);` resulting in an out-of-bounds heap read.

### Reproduction
[POC](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/CVE-2026-117068/suci_oob_poc.py)
```sh
pip install pysctp pycrate
python3 suci_oob_poc.py \
    --host <AMF_NGAP_IP> \
    --port 38412 \
    --ielen 7 \
    --repeat 20000
# Wait a minute
docker inspect oai-amf \
--format '{{.State.Status}} ExitCode={{.State.ExitCode}}'
# Output:
# exited ExitCode=139
```
### Impact

An attacker capable of sending NGAP messages to the AMF can repeatedly  send crafted Registration Requests and terminate the AMF process.
- AMF control-plane service unavailable
- Existing UE registrations are interrupted
- New UE registration requests cannot be processed until recovery
### Weaknesses
-  CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
- CWE-191: Integer Underflow
